meta.title: Logistic Regression vs.\ Gradient Boosting on an Anonymised Tabular Dataset
meta.name: <FULL NAME>

abstract: \textbf{Summary.} We predict the binary \texttt{label} (positive class \texttt{yes}, [[P/minority_share|pct1]] of training rows) from 15 anonymised features and compare an L2-regularised Logistic Regression (LR) with Histogram Gradient Boosting (HGB). HGB ranks positives better (test AP [[R/models/hgb/test/average_precision|3]] vs.\ [[R/models/lr/test/average_precision|3]], 95\% CI of the difference [[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/average_precision/ci/0|+3]] to [[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/average_precision/ci/1|+3]]), but at the tuned operating points the two are statistically tied on F1: the signal is largely additive, and threshold choice matters more than model choice.
issues_table: Dropped: a label cannot be imputed without inventing ground truth.
Primary metric AP; \texttt{class\_weight} searched; threshold tuned on out-of-fold predictions; no resampling.
at most 7 cells per column; [[P/missing/rows_with_any_missing_train|int]] train rows affected
Numeric: median + missing indicator; categorical: own \texttt{\_\_missing\_\_} level. Fitted per CV fold.
0 $\to$ NaN + indicator, on prior grounds (isolates the group in one binary feature, removes a point mass). Ablations A1/A2 show no measurable effect.
Rows kept (test has the same extremes). LR only: winsorise at fold-learned [[L/models/0/preprocess/clip_quantiles/q/0|pct1]]/[[L/models/0/preprocess/clip_quantiles/q/1|pct1]] quantiles (A3).
LR: drop (perfectly collinear, non-identifiable). HGB: keep (trees cannot form linear combinations) (A4, A5).
Pool levels below [[L/rare_level_threshold/value|pct0]] (too few rows for a stable one-hot coefficient); keep Other/Unknown as levels because their positive rates differ from the base rate.
Keep; regularisation copes. Caveat: coefficients and importances are shared.
data:
The training file has [[P/load/raw_train_rows|int]] rows and the test file [[P/load/raw_test_rows|int]]; each has 15 features (7 numeric, 8 categorical) with obfuscated names, so every decision rests on statistics rather than domain knowledge. The profiler (column statistics, single-feature AUCs, linear-redundancy, zero-block and drift detectors) raised [[P/n_flags|int]] flags (Table~\ref{tab:issues}). Train and test distributions match (all KS statistics $\le$ 0.009, no unseen levels), so the provided split is used unchanged. Two findings shaped the plan. First, \texttt{composite\_rank} is an exact weighted sum of two other columns. Second, zeros occur in blocks: the [[P/zero_blocks/0/rows|int]]-row block is entirely negative, which looks structural (e.g.\ ``nothing recorded''). No single feature exceeds AUC [[P/single_feature_auc/instrument|3]], so there is no sign of label leakage, but this block could encode post-outcome information. Outliers were never deleted: the test set has the same extremes, so removing them would make CV optimistic.
%%issues_table%%
features: No column is dropped globally; decisions differ by model because their inductive biases differ. \emph{LR} drops \texttt{composite\_rank} (it adds no information to a linear model and makes the coefficients non-identifiable), winsorises the three heavy-tailed columns, one-hot encodes categoricals after pooling levels below [[L/rare_level_threshold/value|pct0]] into one \emph{infrequent} level, and standardises ([[R/models/lr/n_features_after_preprocessing|int]] inputs incl.\ indicators). \emph{HGB} keeps \texttt{composite\_rank}, because axis-aligned splits cannot synthesise a linear combination; it needs no scaling or clipping (splits depend only on ranks) and uses native categorical splits on the same pooled levels ([[R/models/hgb/n_features_after_preprocessing|int]] inputs). Both models get the zero$\to$NaN + indicator treatment and an own level for missing categories. Deliberately \emph{not} done: target encoding (at most 21 levels; pooling suffices), SMOTE (class weighting and threshold tuning handle imbalance without synthetic points), and importance-based feature selection (it would reuse the data that evaluate it).
training:
\textbf{Why this pair.} The comparison asks whether the label is explained by additive effects (LR) or needs interactions and non-linear thresholds (HGB). Rejected alternatives: an RBF-SVM (no native probabilities, $O(n^2)$ training at 31k rows), $k$-NN (distances over [[R/models/lr/n_features_after_preprocessing|int]] mixed one-hot dimensions are poorly scaled), a single tree (dominated by boosting).
\textbf{Protocol.} Stratified [[L/cv/folds|int]]-fold CV on the training set only; randomised search with [[R/models/lr/n_candidates|int]] (LR) and [[R/models/hgb/n_candidates|int]] (HGB) candidates, refit on average precision (threshold-free and focused on the minority class, unlike accuracy, which the 76\% majority baseline already scores well on), with \texttt{class\_weight}$\in\{$none, balanced$\}$ searched for both (none won). \textbf{Stopping criteria:} LR runs L-BFGS to gradient tolerance $10^{-4}$ (converged after [[R/models/lr/fit/n_iter|int]] of [[R/models/lr/fit/max_iter|int]] iterations); HGB stops when validation log-loss on an internal 10\% split fails to improve for 30 rounds ([[R/models/hgb/fit/n_iter|int]] of [[R/models/hgb/fit/max_iter|int]] rounds). \textbf{Threshold:} the probability cut-off that maximises positive-class F1 on out-of-fold training predictions ([[R/models/lr/oof/threshold|2]] for LR, [[R/models/hgb/oof/threshold|2]] for HGB); the test set is never used for any choice. No selected value lies on a search-range boundary, and the CV train--validation AP gap is small (LR [[R/models/lr/overfit_gap_primary|3]], HGB [[R/models/hgb/overfit_gap_primary|3]]), so over-fitting is limited (larger for HGB, as expected from its capacity).

evaluation:
%%results_table%%
%%figure%%
Both models far exceed the prior (AP [[R/baseline/test/average_precision|3]]). HGB is ahead on the threshold-free metrics: the test AP difference is [[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/average_precision/mean|+3]] (bootstrap $p$=[[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/average_precision/p_two_sided|p]]), consistent with CV ([[R/comparison/cv_corrected_ttest/mean_diff|+3]], corrected $t$-test $p$=[[R/comparison/cv_corrected_ttest/p|p]]). At the tuned thresholds the classifiers disagree on [[R/comparison/mcnemar/A_right_B_wrong|int]]\,+\,[[R/comparison/mcnemar/A_wrong_B_right|int]] test rows and HGB is right on [[R/comparison/mcnemar/A_wrong_B_right|int]] of them (McNemar $p$ [[R/comparison/mcnemar/p_exact|p]]), yet positive-class F1 (CI [[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/f1/ci/0|+3]] to [[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/f1/ci/1|+3]]) and balanced accuracy (CI [[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/balanced_accuracy/ci/0|+3]] to [[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/balanced_accuracy/ci/1|+3]]) are statistically tied: HGB's edge lies in ranking, not at the chosen operating point, and is practically small (about one AP point). Threshold tuning matters more than the model: moving LR from 0.5 to [[R/models/lr/oof/threshold|2]] raises test F1 from [[R/models/lr/test/at_0.5/f1|3]] to [[R/models/lr/test/at_tuned/f1|3]] by trading precision ([[R/models/lr/test/at_0.5/precision|3]]$\to$[[R/models/lr/test/at_tuned/precision|3]]) for recall ([[R/models/lr/test/at_0.5/recall|3]]$\to$[[R/models/lr/test/at_tuned/recall|3]]); at the tuned thresholds LR misses [[R/models/lr/test/at_tuned/confusion/1/0|int]] and HGB [[R/models/hgb/test/at_tuned/confusion/1/0|int]] of [[P/target_test/yes|int]] test positives (Fig.~\ref{fig:results}), at the cost of more false alarms.
%%ablation_table%%
findings:
\textbf{(1) The signal appears largely additive.} A linear model on one-hot features comes within about one AP point of boosting, so interactions and non-linear thresholds add little here (with the caveat that the two pipelines also differ in preprocessing). \textbf{(2) Few preprocessing decisions mattered.} Reverting native categorical splits to one-hot changed HGB AP by [[R/ablations/5/delta|+4]] (A6, $p$=[[R/ablations/5/corrected_ttest/p|p]]); removing LR's winsorising changed AP by [[R/ablations/2/delta|+4]] (A3: beyond fold noise but $p$=[[R/ablations/2/corrected_ttest/p|p]], weak evidence); zero handling (A1, A2) and the \texttt{composite\_rank} choice (A4, A5) changed AP by less than the fold-to-fold noise. The plan predicted that HGB would profit from \texttt{composite\_rank}; the ablation does not support this, even though permutation importance ranks it second for HGB ([[R/models/hgb/permutation_importance/top/1/mean|3]]). Its information is shared with \texttt{aptitude\_score} and \texttt{performance\_score}: important is not the same as necessary. \textbf{(3) The models read the data differently.} LR leans on \texttt{stability\_index} (importance [[R/models/lr/permutation_importance/top/0/mean|3]]), whereas HGB spreads importance over categoricals (\texttt{personal\_interest}, \texttt{instrument}); \texttt{geological\_era}, \texttt{load\_ratio} and \texttt{index\_weight} contribute nothing to HGB.
\textbf{Limitations.} One train/test split; thresholds chosen on the folds that chose hyper-parameters (mildly optimistic); F1 is arbitrary without error costs; anonymised features rule out a domain check of the zero blocks. \textbf{Next steps:} LR with spline features, to separate non-linear main effects from interactions, and a cost-based threshold once costs are known. \textbf{Recommendation:} if transparency matters, LR gives up little; otherwise HGB, tuned to the operating point the application needs.
figure_caption: Held-out test set. (a) Precision--recall curves; dots mark the out-of-fold-tuned operating points, the dashed line the prior. (b, c) Confusion matrices at the tuned thresholds (counts and row-normalised rates).
